title: gondolom: Three Ways to Open an Opinion

sections.title: A third way in, with its own flavour
sections.content: gondolom ("I think, I guess, I suppose") comes from gondol ("to think"), also in its definite form. It sits at the front or end of a sentence exactly like szerintem and azt hiszem, but it leans a little more toward a guess or an inference — something you'd say when you're reasoning from what you can see, not stating a firm view.

sections.title: Three ways to say "I think"
rows: in my opinion (the most neutral, most common)
I think, I believe (a little more tentative)
I guess, I'd think (often a reasoned guess)

items.spanish: Fáradt vagy, gondolom, hosszú napod volt.
items.english: You're tired — I guess you had a long day.

items.spanish: Szerintem finom ez az étel, de gondolom, te másképp gondolod.
items.english: I think this food is tasty, but I guess you think differently.

sections.content: All three openers are largely interchangeable in everyday speech — reach for szerintem by default, and use azt hiszem or gondolom when you want to sound a little less certain, or when you're guessing at a reason rather than stating a taste.
